<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 260|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIIII.}}</noinclude>name, that wil I doe: ⊣ that the Father may be glorified in the Sonne. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in a votiue Masse for the election of the Pope, & vpon Whitsun eue.}}If you aske me any thing in my name, that wil I doe. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=15}}† If you {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is then possible both to loue Christ, and to keepe his cōmaundements.}}∷ loue me, keepe my commaundements. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}}† And I wil aske the father, and he vvil giue you an other c {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Paraclete'' by interpretation is either a comforter, or an aduocate: and therfore to translate it by any one of them only, is ꝑhaps to abridge the sense of this place.}}∷ Paraclete, that he may abide vvith you {{sup|‖}} for euer, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}}† {{sup|‖}} the Spirit of truth, vvhom the vvorld can not receiue, because it seeth him not, neither knovveth him, but you {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`shal knovv''}}`knovv' him: because he shal abide vvith you, and shal be in you. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=18}}† I vvil not leaue you orphanes: I vvil come to you. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=19}}† Yet a litle vvhile: and the vvorld seeth me no more. But you see me: because I liue, and you shal liue.⊣ {{verse|chapter=14|verse=20}}† In that day you shal knovv that I am in my father, and you in me, and I in you. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=21}}† He that hath my commaundements, and keepeth them: he it is that loueth me. And he that loueth me, shal be loued of my father: and I vvil loue him, and vvil manifest my self to him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=22}}† Iudas saith to him, not that Iscariote, Lord, vvhat is done, that thou vvilt manifest thy self to vs, and not to the vvorld? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Whitsunday. And in a Votiue Masse of the holy Ghost.}}{{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to him, If any loue me, he vvil keepe my vvord, and my father vvil loue him, and vve vvil come to him, and vvil make abode vvith him. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=24}}† He that loueth me not, keepeth not my vvordes. And the vvord vvhich you haue heard, is not mine: but his that sent me, the Fathers. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=25}}† These things haue I spoken to you abiding vvith you. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=26}}† But the Paraclete the holy Ghost, vvhom the Father vvil send in my name, he shal {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annot. vpon the 16 Chap. vs. 12 & 13.}}∷ teach you al things, & suggest vnto you al things vvhatsoeuer I shal say to you. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=27}}† Peace I leaue to you, my peace I giue to you. not as the vvorld giueth, doe I giue to you. Let not your hart be troubled, nor feare. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=28}}† You haue heard that I said to you, I goe and I come to you. If you loued me, you vvould be glad verily, that I goe to the Father: because the {{sup|‖}} Father is greater then I. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=29}}† And novv I haue told you before it come to passe: that vvhen it shal come to passe, you may beleeue. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=30}}† Novv I vvil not speake many things vvith you. for the prince of this vvorld commeth, and in me he hath not any thing. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=31}}† But that the vvorld may knovv that I loue the Father: and as the Father hath giuen me commaundement, so doe I: ⊣ Arise, let vs goe hence.<noinclude>{{rh|||ANNOT.}}</noinclude>
